com-mingo , minxi, minctum, 3, v. a.,
I.to pollute, defile: lectum potus (by vomiting), * Hor. S. 1, 3, 90: “suavia comminxit spurcā salivā tuā,” Cat. 78, 8 ; cf. id. 99, 10: commictum caenum, as a term of reproach, for a paltry, dirty fellow: “commictum caeno stercilinium publicum,” Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 3 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
